- PGPPublicKey.join, and with it PGPPublicKeyRing.join and OpenPGPCertificate.join, took two signatures for copies of one another when their signature values matched, and kept the one it already held. A copy of a genuine revocation with its signature type or hashed subpackets rewritten and the signature value left as it was no longer verifies but still matched, so once it had been merged, or when it came first in the same update, the genuine revocation was discarded as its duplicate and the key, subkey or user ID stayed usable. Two signatures are now merged only when they differ in no more than their unhashed subpackets, and PGPSignature.join refuses any other pair. The merge also added to the user ID signature lists of the key it was given, changing the first ring passed to PGPPublicKeyRing.join (github #2508), and lost the value of a version 4 signature carried as a native encoding rather than as MPIs (Ed25519), so that merging a version 4 Ed25519 certificate with a copy of itself gave a ring that could not be encoded; both are corrected.

- PGPPublicKeyRing.join and PGPPublicKey.join, which merge a certificate with another copy of it (OpenPGPCertificate.join merges through them), matched each signature of the copy by scanning the signatures already held, every comparison re-encoding the hashed subpackets and signature value of both, so a merge was quadratic in the number of signatures: two copies of one user ID carrying 20,000 distinct third-party certifications each took over a minute to merge, and anyone can attach certifications to a certificate on a keyserver, as the 2019 flooding of SKS certificates did by the tens of thousands. PGPSignature.join, which a merge applies to every signature both copies carry, likewise scanned the first signature's unhashed subpackets - an area the signature does not cover, so one anyone can fill - for each of the second's, about half a second per shared signature for two full areas, and PGPPublicKeyRing.join looked each key of the first certificate up in the second by a scan. The signatures already held are now indexed once by what two copies of a signature share, the user IDs by value, the second certificate's keys by key ID and the unhashed subpackets through a set. The indexes are ordered trees rather than hash tables: a merge never verifies a signature, so a flooded copy can give every certification one signature value, a user attribute of two identical subpackets hashes to zero, and the hash of a user ID or subpacket's bytes admits multicollisions, any of which drives a hash table's lookups into its collision fallback and the merge back to quadratic. A merge is now O(n log n) in the signatures, user IDs and subpackets of the two copies on every JRE. The merged certificate carries the same content in the same order as before, except that the keys only the second certificate carries now follow in the order it carries them rather than in hash order; the jdk1.3 distribution's PGPPublicKeyRing.join does the same.

- org.bouncycastle.mime.Headers joined folded header lines by String concatenation, copying the whole header accumulated so far for every continuation line, so parsing a long folded header was quadratic in its length: a 1 MB header block of short continuation lines in a message given to BasicMimeParser or the S/MIME parsers took about 17 seconds of CPU, and the block is unbounded. The lines are now appended to a StringBuilder, with the same resulting header values.

-- The ASN.1 parsers for the SEQUENCE types in the X.509, PKCS, OCSP, CMS, CRMF, CMP, ESF, TSP, EAC, DVCS, CMC and ESS packages, and some in the BC, X9 and UA packages, accepted optional fields more than once or out of definition order, and many did not check a tagged field's tag number or ignored elements after the last field. Where a field was repeated, one copy silently replaced the other: a TBSCertificate with two extensions blocks parsed using the first, which also got round the duplicate-extension check, and a second signerInfos SET in a CMS or PKCS#7 SignedData, a repeated PKIMessage protection, and a repeated TSTInfo nonce or accuracy each replaced the first; an OCSPRequest, OCSPResponse or Request with an extra element silently dropped its optionalSignature, responseBytes or singleRequestExtensions, and a TBSRequest its requestExtensions; and an EAC CV certificate accepted its body and signature in either order and more than once, the last copy being used, and its body's data objects in any order; and DVCSCertInfo silently ignored a trailing element that did not parse as Extensions. Each optional field is now accepted at most once, in definition order and with its tag checked, and anything left over is rejected; TBSCertificate.reviewStructure() reports the same problems. RecipientKeyIdentifier also read an OtherKeyAttribute given without a date from the wrong position, and SigPolicyQualifierInfo failed with an ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException when its qualifier was missing. Relates to github #2516.

+- The ASN.1 parsers for the SEQUENCE types in the X.509, PKCS, OCSP, CMS, CRMF, CMP, ESF, TSP, EAC, DVCS, CMC and ESS packages, and some in the BC, X9 and UA packages, accepted optional fields more than once or out of definition order, and many did not check a tagged field's tag number or ignored elements after the last field. Where a field was repeated, one copy silently replaced the other: a TBSCertificate with two extensions blocks parsed using the first, which also got round the duplicate-extension check, and a second signerInfos SET in a CMS or PKCS#7 SignedData, a repeated PKIMessage protection, and a repeated TSTInfo nonce or accuracy each replaced the first; an OCSPRequest, OCSPResponse or Request with an extra element silently dropped its optionalSignature, responseBytes or singleRequestExtensions, and a TBSRequest its requestExtensions; and an EAC CV certificate accepted its body and signature in either order and more than once, the last copy being used, and its body's data objects in any order; and DVCSCertInfo silently ignored a trailing element that did not parse as Extensions. Each optional field is now accepted at most once, in definition order and with its tag checked, and anything left over is rejected; TBSCertificate.reviewStructure() reports the same problems. RecipientKeyIdentifier also read an OtherKeyAttribute given without a date from the wrong position, and SigPolicyQualifierInfo failed with an ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException when its qualifier was missing. The GOST 28147/R 34.10 transport types, ECC-CMS-SharedInfo, MQVuserKeyingMaterial, IetfAttrSyntax, the SigI PersonalData, the ISIS-MTT NamingAuthority, ProfessionInfo and ProcurationSyntax, and the deprecated X509Extensions now follow the same rules, ProcurationSyntax requiring its signingFor field, and the streaming SignedData, EnvelopedData, AuthEnvelopedData and AuthenticatedData parsers reject an element after their last field once it has been read, with AuthenticatedDataParser now checking the digestAlgorithm tag; the IetfAttrSyntax acceptance of an untagged policyAuthority, as written by VOMS, is kept. Relates to github #2516.

- KeyStore.load() with a null stream, which KeyStore specifies as making the store empty, left a loaded PKCS12 store's entries and MAC settings in place, and the JKS reader's entries too; the JKS reader also added each file's certificates to those of the last. A load that failed part way through - a damaged file, or a wrong password the store only detects after reading its contents - left the PKCS12, BKS, UBER, BCFKS and JKS stores emptied or half replaced, and the stores that pick between JKS and their own format switched to the other format's contents. Every BC key store now empties on a null load and replaces its contents on a successful one, and a load that fails leaves the store as it was, as the JDK's own key stores do.

- An MLS Commit could not replace a group member in one epoch: each Add proposal's KeyPackage was validated against the tree before the commit, where the member being removed is still present, so a KeyPackage keeping the removed member's signature key failed the leaf-node uniqueness check and the proposal list was rejected by committer and receivers alike, although RFC 9420 sec. 12.2 permits an Add for a client already in the group when the same proposal list removes the matching client. An Add may now repeat the signature key of a leaf that a valid Remove in the same list takes out of the tree, provided the credential is identical; the KeyPackage's init and leaf encryption keys must still be new, and duplicate Adds, a Remove paired with an Update of the same leaf, and an Add matching a member the list does not remove are rejected as before. Relates to github #2504.

- LDAPUtils.parseDN, which X509LDAPCertStoreSpi and LDAPStoreHelper use to take the search value for a certificate or CRL lookup from a DN, found the attribute by its bare name anywhere in the DN, so the name could match inside another attribute's value: with the default "o" attribute, "CN=Bob Root CA, O=Example" was searched for as "b Root CA" and the lookup missed, and a DN with an empty value ("O=x, CN=") or a value ending in the attribute name ("O=cn, L=y") threw StringIndexOutOfBoundsException out of the CertStore. With revocation checking a missed CRL fails validation, or with PKIXRevocationChecker.Option.SOFT_FAIL is silently skipped. For LDAPStoreHelper this was a regression in 1.86, which replaced its own parser, requiring the "=", with the shared one. The attribute is now only taken as the type of an RDN component and an empty value gives an empty search value. The value is read as the component's value, ending at an unescaped ',' or '+' outside a quoted string, so a quoted value keeps its commas, a multi-valued RDN gives the one attribute's value, and both the RFC 2253 and the RFC 1779 forms the stores pass are read. The escapes of the DN string form, a `\` before a character or before two hex digits of UTF-8, are now decoded before the value is escaped for the filter, so a value such as `Smith\, John` is searched for as stored rather than with a literal backslash. The jdk1.4 LDAPStoreHelper now uses the same parser in place of its own copy, which had the same empty-value failure (github #2511).
